client.industry_secondary: Mobile and in-shop truck service centers
client.business_model: Nationwide network of mobile technicians and service centers providing preventative maintenance and repair for medium- and heavy-duty truck fleets
client.sponsor_pe_firm: Ares Management Corporation (majority owner, acquired April 2025)
client.client_history: Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, Epika Fleet Services has grown through ten+ acquisitions into a coast-to-coast provider serving more than 2,000 fleet customers across nearly 40 states.

revenue.notes: Company does not publicly disclose revenue. Growjo estimates ~$18 M. No corroborating figures found in press releases or filings.

locations.notes: Release states 'approximately 20 in-shop centers'. Mobile branches and quick-service sites are additional but not clearly enumerated; physical in-shop facilities most comparable to 'locations' metric requested.

employees.source: Epika press release announcing Ares acquisition (epikafleet.com/press-release/epika-fleet-services-inc-acquired-by-ares-management, 2025-04-21)
employees.notes: Press release cites 'more than 550 technicians'; LinkedIn company page lists ~600 total employees (accessed 2026-02-02). Using 550 as conservative figure.

extraction_sources: Agreement/Treya Procurement Cost Reduction Services Agreement_Epika Fleet Services_vF_8.26.24.pdf
PR Newswire – partnership with Fleet Mobile Maintenance (2023-10-06)
extraction_notes: Official legal name confirmed in services agreement between Treya Partners and Epika Fleet Services, Inc.
PE ownership: Trivest was minority investor (2018) but majority stake now held by Ares Management as confirmed by multiple press releases; Ares reported as current sponsor.
Revenue is an external estimate only; no primary documents list dollar figures.
Employee count varies slightly by source (550+ in 2025 press release vs ~600 on LinkedIn); treated as medium confidence.
Physical location count refers to in-shop centers; total service touch-points (mobile branches, quick-service, etc.) are higher but inconsistently reported.
